newsitem.title: USA: Fla. consumer confidence drops, buying continues.
newsitem.headline: Fla. consumer confidence drops, buying continues.

text.p: Florida's overall consumer confidence dropped two percentage points in April, but the perception that now is a good time to buy big-ticket items rose by two percentage points, University of Florida economists said Tuesday.
A surging dollar abroad and better pay at home encouraged many Florida residents that now is a good time to buy expensive items such as cars, appliances and furniture.

"Consumers may be shopping for good deals, but they are not yet retreating in their spending," said Chris McCarty, survey director for the university's Bureau of Economic and Business Research. "Inflation remains low and the quarter-point rise in interest rates has not affected consumers yet."
The overall drop in confidence still leaves the index at 95, the fourth consecutive month it has registered at that level or above.
Respondents' perception of their personal finances fell to 89 in April from 95 in March.
The economists said the March figure was an aberration in a year when that component of the index was consistently below 90.
Resondents who reported their personal finances to be worse than they were a year ago cited employer downsizing, inflation and poor health as the main reasons.

The fall in the personal finance component was balanced by the increase in the perception that now is a good time to buy big-ticket items, and by a one-point rise in the outlook for personal financial conditions a year from now.
Employed Floridians gave pessimistic reports about April business conditions.

Fifty-two percent said business was better than a year ago, down from 56 percent in March. The share expecting extra employees to be hired at their workplace in the next six months fell to 34 in April from 36 in March.
The monthly consumer survey was based on telephone interviews with 974 randomly selected Florida adults and has an error margin of about three points.
